q: 1. The construction works costing below rupees twenty thousand are classified as ............
explain: Small-scale works with low financial thresholds (like Rs. 20,000) are typically categorized as 'Minor Works' for administrative and accounting purposes.

q: 2. The construction costing above rupees one lac are classified as ............
explain: Works exceeding a certain financial threshold (often Rs. 100,000 or 1 Lac) are typically classified as 'Projects' requiring detailed planning and approval.

q: 3. The project technical audit is done ............
explain: A technical audit is primarily conducted once the project is physically complete to verify that all technical specifications were followed and quality standards were met.

the total sum to be paid to the municipal authorities by the tenants
a part of the money kept in reserve for providing additional structure and structural modifications
explain: A sinking fund is a sum set aside periodically so that at the end of the utility period of the asset, sufficient funds are available for its replacement.

q: 5. The amount saved as depreciation reserve fund will be termed as ............
explain: Depreciation is an internal accounting provision for the wear and tear of an asset; it is not classified as profit, loss, or direct operating cost in this context.

q: 6. With the usual notations, sinking fund factor is given by .............
explain: The sinking fund factor is the amount of money to be set aside annually to accumulate a certain sum of money at the end of a given period at a given interest rate.
